cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: The 4 Cs of food safety are: Cross-contamination prevention, Cleaning, Chilling, and Cooking.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Cross-contamination prevention: use separate boards, wash hands after handling raw meat, store raw foods below cooked foods.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Cleaning: wash and disinfect all surfaces, equipment, and hands before and after food preparation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Chilling: keep the fridge at 0–5°C, the freezer at −18°C or below; never put hot food directly in the fridge.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Cooking: food must reach a core temperature of at least 75°C (UK) or 70°C for 2 minutes (EU); use a food thermometer to check.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Personal hygiene includes: washing hands with soap and warm water, tying back hair, wearing a clean apron, covering cuts with blue waterproof plasters, and not working when ill.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: The correct handwashing technique involves: wet hands, apply soap, rub palms, backs, between fingers, thumbs, and wrists for at least 20 seconds, rinse, and dry with a clean towel.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Kitchen design for food safety: separate raw and cooked preparation areas, easy-to-clean surfaces, non-slip flooring, good lighting and ventilation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: Safe food storage: raw meat on the bottom shelf of the fridge, dairy in the middle, cooked foods on top, fruit and vegetables in the crisper drawer.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Food Hygiene & Safe Practice
cards.back: The 90-minute rule: food should not be left in the danger zone (5–63°C) for more than 90 minutes total; cool cooked food rapidly and refrigerate within 1–2 hours.

cards.front: What should you know about food preparation & nutrition exam tips — food hygiene & safe practice?
cards.back: 1. For Food Hygiene & Safe Practice questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2. Check your answer makes sense in context (estimation, units, reasonableness) 3. Use correct mathematical notation and state formulae before substituting values 4. If a Food Hygiene & Safe Practice question asks you to 'prove' or 'show', write a logical chain of reasoning with a conclusion line 5. For problem-solving, identify the topic first, then recall the relevant method
